notes.summary: For G331’s unchanged geometric class, continuous-obstacle raw C and D envelopes agree. Their positivity is equivalent to continuity; neither is automatic.
notes.detailedSummary: Registers the qualified G331 cone, comparison and full conductor descent without importing an envelope theorem. Compact directed-cover arguments prove that finite continuous D functions belong to C, that continuous-obstacle C and D suprema coincide, and that their common bounded lower semicontinuous supremum belongs to the geometric class exactly when continuous. Raw envelopes are nonexpansive in uniform norm.
notes.text:
Register G331 exactly as the sole incoming correctness/source grant. Its complete incoming text, mandatory qualifications and source ledger are retained unchanged in G331-qualified-grant.json. The unchanged entire original task, family dossier and completionCriteria are in original-task.json. Other packet files are DATA, not additional theorem grants.

For an excellent local ring R, reduce nilpotents and fix a proper primary ideal a. Let X=V_a(R), retaining every semivaluation support prime strictly below the maximal ideal. G331 supplies the independent geometric core on directed actual primary blowups: actual negative effective finite REAL Cartier presentations having nonnegative degree on EVERY contracted proper integral curve. Its uniform closure C and actual decreasing-net completion D satisfy C_geom=C_ideal and D_geom=D_ideal. No arbitrary-model cofinality, increasing-limit closure, envelope, product or energy theorem is granted. Dimension-zero local reduction has the empty boundary.

C is a uniformly closed convex cone of finite continuous nonpositive functions, stable under finite maxima and containing every nonpositive constant. D consists of infima of nonempty decreasing C-nets, with bottom included. G331 also supplies exact positive C and D normalization descent through FULL restriction fibres: singleton fibres at finite conductor value, and precisely conductor-quotient fibres at infinite value. Its BFJ identification applies only at smooth affine CLOSED germs over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields, with direct DVR/empty cases.

Every u=inf_i u_i in D is upper semicontinuous: {u<t}=union_i{u_i<t}. If u is finite continuous, then u belongs to C. For epsilon>0, the open sets {u_i<u+epsilon} cover compact X; directedness and a finite subcover select one common term satisfying u<=u_i<u+epsilon everywhere. Uniform closedness proves membership in C. Subtraction of a nonnegative constant preserves C and D. Finite maxima in D follow by taking the product directed set of representing nets; simultaneous strict upper tests prove convergence to the maximum of their limits, including bottom values.

Define the raw supremum P_D phi(v)=sup{u(v):u in D, u<=phi}. Bottom makes the family nonempty. For finite continuous phi, define P_C similarly; negative constants make both suprema finite and bounded.

For every finite continuous obstacle on every germ in the grant, P_D phi=P_C phi. Indeed, if u=inf_i u_i<=phi, compactness of the open cover {u_i<phi+epsilon} selects a common term. Then u_i-epsilon belongs to C and lies below phi, giving P_C phi>=u-epsilon. Send epsilon to zero and take the supremum over u. This proof includes unbounded and partially bottom D-minorants.

The common supremum is lower semicontinuous. It belongs to D if and only if it is continuous, equivalently if and only if it belongs to C. D membership supplies upper semicontinuity; the preceding finite-continuous D-to-C argument applies. Conversely, if the raw supremum is continuous, the open sets {g>P_C phi-epsilon}, for admissible g in C, cover X. A finite maximum gives a uniform approximation from below, and closedness of C establishes membership. Thus a greatest geometric minorant exists for a continuous obstacle exactly when its raw supremum is continuous. This is a criterion for the unchanged cone, not a definition of a new envelope-positive subcone.

Raw continuous-obstacle envelopes satisfy ||P_D phi-P_D psi||_infinity<=||phi-psi||_infinity. If phi<=psi+epsilon, shifting each admissible minorant down by epsilon gives P_D phi-epsilon<=P_D psi; reverse the roles. Monotonicity, positive homogeneity for positive scalars, and replacing an obstacle by min(phi,0) follow directly from the admissible families. These order identities alone imply no positivity.

notes.summary: An explicit continuous obstacle on the excellent nonnormal surface xy=0 has no maximal G331-geometric minorant. Its raw supremum and usc regularization both fail positivity.
notes.detailedSummary: The two smooth normalization boundaries identify their conductor line-support points. A continuous fibre-compatible obstacle forces every minorant on the second branch to be at most −2. Positively descended primary-ideal tuples approach −1 on the first branch away from the identified point while retaining −2 there. The exact supremum is not usc. Finite maxima strictly improve every admissible minorant. Its usc regularization violates the second branch’s ideal-order inequality. This is a boundary-cone counterexample, distinct from the prior literal radial obstruction.
notes.text:
Work over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k. Set R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy), with maximal-ideal gauge. This is a reduced excellent nonnormal local surface. Its finite normalization is S=A times B, where A=k[x,z]_(x,z), B=k[y,z]_(y,z). Explicitly R=A times_T B for T=k[z]_(z), using x=0 and y=0. Polynomial pairs with equal restrictions are represented by f(x,z)+g(y,z)-h(z); clearing local unit denominators proves the localized identity. The two idempotents generate S as a finite R-module, and each factor is normal with the appropriate component fraction field. The conductor is (x)A times (y)B=(x,y)R: multiplication by the idempotents tests that both common restrictions vanish.

Let X_A and X_B be the maximal-ideal normalized boundaries. On X_A write a=w(x), b=w(z), so min(a,b)=1. The unique point q_A killing x is ord_z on A/(x); define q_B similarly. G331’s exact conductor quotient identifies precisely q_A with q_B and no other points. At infinite conductor value the quotient is T into T times T, with one normalized DVR order on each factor. Let q be their common image. Its support (x,y) is NONMINIMAL in R.

Define the upstairs obstacle phi_A=-1 and phi_B(w)=-3+min(w(y),2). Truncated evaluation is continuous, including infinite values. Both obstacle values at q_A,q_B equal −1, so the tuple descends through the compact quotient to a finite continuous phi on X_R, valued in [−2,−1].

There is a universal order inequality on B. For o_B=ord_(y,z), every normalized w satisfies w(f)>=o_B(f), since f in (y,z)^d implies w(f)>=d. Therefore negative primary-ideal profiles satisfy g(w)<=g(o_B). Uniform limits and actual decreasing limits preserve this inequality, so by the accepted comparison it holds for every g in D_B. Since phi_B(o_B)=−2, every downstairs geometric minorant pulls back to a function <=−2 on ALL of X_B, hence has value <=−2 at q.

For n>=1, take the actual proper primary A-ideal J_n=(x^n,x z^(n−1),z^(2n)). Define u_n,A=−w(J_n)/n and u_n,B=−2. The first is an actual ideal profile in C_A; the second is a primary-gauge constant in C_B. Both equal −2 at the identified pair. G331’s positive C-descent establishes u_n in C_geom,R BEFORE any envelope inference.

On X_A the formula is u_n,A=−min{a,(a+(n−1)b)/n,2b}. When n=1 the middle monomial is x, even if b is infinite; no undefined zero-times-infinity arithmetic is used. Every entry has value at least one, so u_n,A<=−1. Also −2<=phi_B. Thus each u_n is an admissible positive continuous minorant.

These minorants increase on the ENTIRE boundary. If a<=b, then a=1 and their values are identically −1. If a>b, then b=1. For finite a, min{a,1+(a−1)/n,2} decreases to one. For a=infinity, the unique point is q_A and the minimum remains two. Consequently their supremum h is −1 on X_A minus q_A, −2 at q_A, and −2 everywhere on X_B.

This h is exactly P_D phi=P_C phi. The obstacle bounds every A-minorant by −1; the proved B order inequality bounds every B-minorant by −2, including q. Those are precisely h’s upper bounds. The already positive u_n give the matching pointwise lower bounds.

For integers L>=1, take the monomial valuation w_L(x)=L,w_L(z)=1 on A and restrict it to v_L on R. These converge pointwise to q: positive x-degree terms acquire values tending to infinity, while the x^0 part has its z-order; local unit denominators have value zero. The supports of v_L are (y), while q has support (x,y). Yet h(v_L)=−1 and h(q)=−2. Thus h is not upper semicontinuous and cannot belong to D_geom. No greatest geometric minorant exists.

There is not even a maximal minorant. For any u in D_R below phi, u(q)<=−2. Upper semicontinuity gives a neighbourhood of q where u<−3/2. Choose a finite L>=2 with v_L there. For n>2(L−1), u_n(v_L)=−1−(L−1)/n>−3/2. The finite maximum max(u,u_n) belongs to D_R, remains below phi, and strictly improves u.

The usc regularization h*(v)=inf_{U containing v}sup_U h equals h away from q and equals −1 at q. The branch images are closed and intersect only at q, and v_L converges to q, proving these values. Although h*<=phi, its B-pullback has value −1 at q_B and −2 at o_B, violating g(q_B)<=g(o_B). Hence regularization also fails geometric positivity.

This refutes universal greatest-minorant or usc-regularized envelope positivity for the UNCHANGED G331 class in original excellent/nonnormal scope, even with smooth normalization and a strictly negative bounded continuous obstacle. It does not refute G331’s cone comparison. The essential identified nonminimal-support fibre lies on a positive-dimensional conductor quotient, unlike the prior literal radial curve example.

notes.summary: At the published smooth BFJ hypotheses, every finite continuous obstacle has an actual continuous geometric envelope.
notes.detailedSummary: Applies the complete BFJ determining-envelope theorem only to smooth affine closed germs over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields. Primary ideals from L-infinity(tW) give an all-support uniform envelope estimate, establishing C membership before geometric positivity. Published piecewise-affine density and the proved raw norm estimate extend the result to arbitrary continuous obstacles.
notes.text:
Assume R is the local ring of a smooth CLOSED point of an affine variety over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, with dimension at least two. Initially use the maximal-ideal gauge. G331 identifies C with the finite continuous BFJ subclass and D with BFJ’s canonical all-semivaluation class, with bottom adjoined.

The sole new essential primary application is Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson, Valuations and Plurisubharmonic Singularities, Publ. RIMS 44 (2008), 449–494. Exact authorized PDF/text bindings, complete immediate reading units and application hypotheses are recorded in source-application-ledger.md and evidence/reading-record.json. Used complete units include the Setting, Sections 1.5–1.7 and their retraction/density proofs, Definition 2.1, Definition 2.5, Proposition 2.7, Definition 2.8, Proposition 3.11 with its closed-simplex continuity proof, and the ENTIRE Section 3.5, including Proposition 3.18 and Lemma 3.22 with their proofs. Historical smooth resolution, multiplier subadditivity and approximation dependencies are disclosed; they are not recursively reread or transferred to singular/positive-characteristic scope.

First let h be finite continuous and determined on one dual complex: h=h composed with r_pi. Choose M>=1 with h>=−M. Let W be the coefficientwise supremum of nef Weil divisors Z<=Z(h). The constant −M is an admissible nef lower bound. Replace candidates by max(Z,−M) and direct finite maxima by finite subsets. Their coefficient limits lie in [−M,0]; BFJ’s weak closed nef cone and finite-max stability establish that W is genuinely nef. This uses the published smooth coefficient cone, not arbitrary increasing closure of singular D.

BFJ 3.11 associates to W a formal psh function H, continuous on every CLOSED simplex, extended to all semivaluations by H(v)=inf_pi' H(r_pi' v). Divisorial inequalities extend to closed simplices by rational-point density and substantive continuity, and then through this canonical infimum. Thus −M<=H<=0. Also H<=h on all supports: on the determining complex W<=Z(h) gives H<=h, and Proposition 2.7 gives H(v)<=H(r_pi v)<=h(r_pi v)=h(v).

Separate W=0, whose function H=0 already lies in C. For W nonzero, the complete BFJ 3.18 theorem gives c>0 and, for k>c, W_k<=W<=(1−c/k)W_(k−c), where W_t=t^−1 Z(L-infinity(tW)). Definition 3.17 gives L-infinity(tW)=L-infinity(tZ(h)), so these ideals encode the original determining obstacle.

Each such ideal contains the completed maximal ideal to exponent ceil(tM), since W>=−M. It is proper when W is nonzero, because a unit has divisor zero and cannot lie below a negative coefficient of tW. Therefore it is primary. For positive integers t, contract it to I_t in R using G331’s exact completion/primary contraction, preserving ALL semivaluation values. Put f_t=−v(I_t)/t in C; then −M−1/t<=f_t<=0.

Take k=t+c in the BFJ estimate. Closed-simplex continuity and canonical all-retraction infima extend both inequalities to every semivaluation. They give

f_t<=H<=t/(t+c) f_t,

and hence

0<=H−f_t<=c/(t+c)(M+1/t).

This is a uniform bound on the entire compact all-support boundary. Consequently H belongs to C by uniform closedness. Only AFTER this membership proof does the accepted comparison identify H as geometrically positive. No Hartogs theorem, arbitrary increasing closure or convexity-only boundary-continuity assertion is used.

H is the actual greatest D-minorant of h. For any nonbottom u in D below h, the granted BFJ identification gives its nef coefficient divisor Z(u)<=Z(h), hence Z(u)<=W. Closed-simplex continuity and canonical retractions yield u<=H everywhere. Bottom is automatic. Therefore P_D h=P_C h=H in C_geom.

The exact source estimate is restricted to its genuine determining-envelope hypotheses. In BFJ’s complete immediate proof, Lemma 3.22 recovers W as sup_t W_t on divisorial points. Smooth multiplier subadditivity yields W<=Z(L2(W)); bounded thinness versus strictly negative nonzero W on the determining complex yields L2(kW) contained in L-infinity((k−c)W). Applying the previous inequality to kW gives the estimate used above. The fourth assertion of 3.18 is not needed. No characteristic-free version of these multiplier estimates is claimed.

BFJ 1.14–1.15 proves uniform density of piecewise affine functions, each determined on one dual complex, in finite continuous functions. Choose h_j uniformly approaching an arbitrary continuous obstacle phi. The RAW norm estimate of n1 gives ||P_D h_j−P_D phi||_infinity tending to zero. Each P_D h_j already belongs to C; closedness proves P_D phi belongs to C. It is admissible and greatest. This establishes continuous envelope positivity for arbitrary continuous obstacles without an unproved increasing-limit step.

For determining obstacles the construction agrees with the published BFJ nef envelope on ALL semivaluations; for arbitrary continuous obstacles it is its uniform extension. Primary-gauge changes are proved in n5. The DVR and empty cases are direct there and in n1. General excellent singular or positive-characteristic envelope positivity is not supplied by this source.

notes.summary: Where continuous envelopes are separately established, every bounded-above extended usc obstacle has a greatest D-geometric minorant through one actual decreasing C-net.
notes.detailedSummary: Constructs the downward-directed net of finite continuous strict majorants of an extended usc obstacle. Their already positive continuous envelopes decrease; the infimum belongs to the original D by definition and is the greatest minorant. This includes bottom and mixed patterns, without nested-net flattening or increasing closure. The hypothesis is proved in the smooth sector and fails in the nonnormal counterexample.
notes.text:
Keep the unchanged G331 cone. Suppose a particular boundary has the continuous envelope property: P_D psi belongs to C for every finite continuous real obstacle psi. This is a separately proved property, not a new positivity definition. N3 establishes it at the published smooth hypotheses; n2 disproves it in general excellent/nonnormal scope.

Let phi:X into [−infinity,M] be upper semicontinuous, with M finite. We construct its actual D-envelope, permitting partial bottom, mixed signs and zeros.

Every such phi is the infimum of an ACTUAL decreasing net of finite continuous strict majorants. Here are the topology details. Compact Hausdorff spaces are normal: pointwise Hausdorff separation of two compact disjoint closed sets, followed by finite subcovers of each, yields disjoint open neighbourhoods. Consequently a closed F inside open U admits F subset O subset closure(O) subset U. Iterating these separations at dyadic rationals produces nested open sets with closure(O_r) subset O_s for r<s. The function inf{r:x in O_r}, with endpoint conventions, is continuous because its strict sublevel and superlevel sets are unions of O_r and complements of closure(O_r). This proves the continuous-cutoff assertion used below.

For a point v and finite t>phi(v), choose finite ell with phi(v)<ell<t, also when phi(v)=−infinity. The set U={phi<ell} is open. Normality and the cutoff construction give continuous chi:X into [0,1] with chi(v)=1 and closed support inside U. Choose M'>max(M,ell) and set F=chi ell+(1−chi)M'. On U both endpoint values strictly exceed phi; outside the support F=M'>phi. Thus F>phi everywhere and F(v)=ell<t.

The family Fcal of all finite continuous functions strictly above phi is nonempty and closed under finite minimum, hence downward directed. The preceding construction proves inf Fcal=phi pointwise. Reverse pointwise order makes it a genuine decreasing net; no countable cofinal sequence is asserted on a nonmetrizable boundary.

For F in Fcal, the assumed continuous-envelope property supplies p_F=P_D F in C, with positivity already established. Monotonicity makes p_F a decreasing C-net. Set u=inf_F p_F. By the original definition of D, u belongs to D. Since p_F<=F, u<=phi. Conversely, if g in D lies below phi, then g<=F for every F, hence g<=P_D F for every F and g<=u. Therefore u=P_D phi is the greatest geometric minorant. The order is membership, obstacle domination, greatestness, then geometric interpretation.

More generally, for any particular decreasing net of finite continuous obstacles phi_i whose envelopes have ALREADY been established in C, the same proof gives P_D(inf_i phi_i)=inf_i P_D phi_i in D. No flattening of D-representations is involved: the approximating envelopes themselves lie in C.

Finite continuous obstacles have finite continuous bounded envelopes on such a domain. General bounded-above extended usc obstacles have nonpositive extended usc envelopes with the actual decreasing continuous positive representation just constructed. No general continuity claim is made for this larger obstacle class. If phi>=0 everywhere, zero is greatest; if phi is identically bottom, bottom is the only minorant. Partial bottom and mixed-zero patterns remain permitted, subject to the granted normal-centre zero dichotomy. The complete curve formulas in n5 include every such pattern.

Thus the result gives a complete bounded-above extended usc obstacle theorem at the smooth BFJ hypotheses, and on any other independently established continuous-envelope sector. It is not asserted for every excellent singular/nonnormal germ.

notes.summary: Exact gauge covariance and fibre-constrained conductor rules; complete geometric clipping on all excellent reduced curves and positive bijective-normalization sectors.
notes.detailedSummary: Primary section changes commute with raw envelopes through the accepted order bijections. Normalization identifies downstairs minorants with the full-fibre-constant upstairs subclass; unconstrained envelopes need not descend. Bijective boundaries with good normalization centres give positive sectors. On every excellent reduced curve, positive descent yields the finite nonpositive geometric orthant, and actual decreasing clipped tuples yield its extended completion. The actual envelope is then min(obstacle,0), including mixed zero and partial bottom.
notes.text:
Use G331’s exact primary-gauge and positive descent rules as registered in n1. No new essential external source theorem is applied here.

For proper primary ideals a,b define T_ab u(v/v(b))=u(v)/v(b), for v in V_a(R), and transform obstacles by the SAME formula. The denominator is positive continuous with bounded inverse. G331 makes T_ab an order bijection on C and D. Pointwise division by a positive number commutes with suprema, so P_D,b(T_ab phi)=T_ab(P_D,a phi), including bottom values. The C formula for continuous obstacles follows identically. Successive factors telescope, giving the exact three-gauge cocycle. Continuity, extended usc regularity, zeros, bottom patterns and class membership are preserved. The counterexample’s discontinuity and nonpositivity therefore survive every primary-gauge change.

Let rho:Xtilde into X be the normalization compact quotient, using aS upstairs and the product classes over ALL local normalization centres. For every obstacle there is an exact raw identity:

rho* P_D,R phi = sup{u in D_S: u<=rho*phi and u is constant on EVERY rho-fibre}.

Downstairs admissible functions pull back to this family; every member of this family descends positively by G331. Equality of admissible families proves the identity without presuming positivity of their supremum. The same C identity holds for finite continuous obstacles.

Full-fibre compatibility means singleton fibres at finite conductor value and equality over R/c into S/c on the entire infinite-conductor stratum. No support prime or zero/bottom pattern is omitted. The fibre constraint cannot be dropped merely because the obstacle is fibre constant. In n2 the unconstrained upstairs envelope is −1 on A and −2 on B, with different values at q_A,q_B. Both centres have the smooth continuous envelope property, but their envelopes fail compatibility.

If an unconstrained upstairs envelope is separately known to belong to D_S AND to be fibre constant, it descends positively and is the downstairs greatest minorant. Every other admissible pullback is dominated upstairs. If the upstairs envelope is continuous, compact quotient descent gives continuity downstairs, hence C membership. Positivity and fibre constancy are actual requirements.

There is a complete positive sector: if rho is bijective and each local normalization centre has the continuous envelope property, compact Hausdorffness makes rho a homeomorphism and removes the compatibility constraint. Componentwise continuous envelopes descend to actual C_R envelopes. N4 then gives D_R envelopes for every bounded-above extended usc obstacle. A primary conductor together with smooth BFJ normalization centres is a sufficient example: primary conductor values are finite at every centred point, so G331 gives bijectivity. Bijectivity itself is the sufficient boundary condition; primary conductor is not claimed necessary.

Now consider ANY excellent reduced local curve germ, in arbitrary characteristic and with arbitrary residue field. Its finite normalization has finitely many local DVR centres S_i above the marked point. The dimension-one normal Noetherian local DVR criterion and finite excellent normalization are ordinary algebraic background already disclosed in G331; no resolution or multiplier approximation is used.

The conductor is primary unless it is the unit ideal. Indeed every nonmaximal prime of a reduced local curve is minimal, and its localization is the generic field. Normalization localizes to the same field. The finite module S/R is supported only at the maximal ideal and is annihilated by a power of that ideal. Hence the conductor contains a maximal-ideal power. Consequently its value is finite at every centred point, and the normalization boundary map is bijective.

On S_i with parameter t_i, every centred semivaluation is a positive multiple of ord_i: every nonzero element is t_i^d times a unit. If b_i=ord_i(aS_i)>0, its normalized section is the singleton ord_i/b_i. Thus the downstairs curve link is the finite discrete set of local normalization CENTRES, not merely minimal components.

Each singleton’s C class consists of all finite nonpositive constants, realized by nonnegative real multiples of the negative parameter-ideal profile and by the unit for zero. The semilocal product class and G331’s positive C-descent therefore prove

C_geom,R=C_ideal,R=(−infinity,0]^r,

where the left endpoint is excluded, so values are finite. Every extended nonpositive tuple h is in D_geom: the already positive finite tuples h_i^(N)=max(h_i,−N) DECREASE to h. Conversely all D functions are nonpositive. Hence D_geom,R=D_ideal,R=[−infinity,0]^r.

Only AFTER these geometric membership results, for every extended obstacle phi in [−infinity,+infinity]^r, define h_i=min(phi_i,0). It belongs to D_geom, lies below phi and dominates every admissible nonpositive tuple. Therefore it is the actual greatest geometric envelope. Finite obstacles give continuous C outputs; extended outputs are usc on the finite link. All-zero, mixed-zero, all-bottom and partial-bottom patterns are explicitly included. The formula agrees with ideal clipping THROUGH the accepted geometric comparison and positive descent, not by relabeling an ideal completion.

Curve primary-gauge changes act by c_i^b=ord_i(a)/ord_i(b) times c_i^a. These positive diagonal factors commute with clipping, including zero and bottom. The smooth DVR case is one singleton; dimension zero is the unique empty function.

For the curve node, (−1,0) is consequently an actual geometric envelope. The prior literal homogeneous logarithmic radial analytic class has a different domain and is not used as a premise or counterexample here. N2 instead uses a positive-dimensional conductor quotient with an identified nonminimal-support boundary pair.

notes.text:
The entire original P12.3, full family dossier and completionCriteria remain unchanged in original-task.json. This deliverable is an unverified mathematical draft with candidate=false. It does not claim a complete positive envelope theory on every excellent singular/nonnormal germ or replace the original target by a radial calculation.

N2 proves a new exact obstruction for the specific independently geometric cone granted by G331. On the excellent nonnormal surface k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy), a continuous obstacle valued in [−2,−1] has no maximal geometric minorant. Its exact raw supremum equals −1 on the first normalization boundary outside the identified conductor point, and −2 there and on the second boundary. It is not usc and therefore not in D_geom. Its usc regularization remains below the obstacle but violates the second smooth branch’s primary-ideal order inequality. Every approximating minorant was positively established in C_geom before its use.

Thus a universal assertion that raw continuous-obstacle suprema, or their usc regularizations, are positive members of the UNCHANGED granted class is false in the original excellent/nonnormal scope. A greatest-minorant envelope satisfying that unrestricted requirement cannot be constructed for this obstacle. No tautologically positive replacement cone, altered support space or deleted conductor fibre is proposed. Other envelope notions or enlarged classes require new constructions and comparison theorems and are not claimed.

N1 identifies the precise missing step: continuous-obstacle raw C and D suprema agree and are bounded lsc and uniformly nonexpansive; membership and greatestness are equivalent to continuity. N3 proves continuity at the published smooth BFJ hypotheses using the exact determining-envelope estimate followed by an all-support uniform approximation and density argument. N4 proves actual decreasing-net D envelopes for bounded-above extended usc obstacles wherever the continuous property is separately established. N5 proves exact primary-gauge covariance, the full constrained conductor rule, complete reduced-curve geometric clipping and the stated bijective-normalization sectors.

The completed positive domains are smooth affine closed BFJ germs over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields, ALL excellent reduced curves in arbitrary characteristic/residue field, and bijective normalization boundaries with continuous-envelope centres. General excellent NORMAL singular envelope continuity is not settled here. Smooth normalization alone is insufficient, as n2 demonstrates.
